title: Investigate Ui React Vitest Heap Out Of Memory
description: `bun x vitest run --config vitest.config.ts` in `ui/js/react/` (the `@semio-tech/ui-react` package, single giant `index.tsx` test file with `import.meta.vitest`, ~6100 lines / 31 describe / 327 it) reliably OOMs with 'Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit'. Unfiltered run crashes ~34min (default heap), ~65min with 8GB heap (316 tests reported), and even a `-t` filtered run selecting ~28/316 tests STILL OOMs after ~21min despite skipping 288 tests — proving the leak isn't proportional to executed test count. Need to determine whether the leak is in test collection/registration (module-level code, describe() bodies executed even for skipped tests) vs per-test execution (React root not unmounted, observer/listener leaks, unbounded module-level caches in the ~25k-line component source above the test block). Goal: find root cause and get `nx run @semio-tech/ui-react:test-long`/`-exhaustive` to complete cleanly.
summary:
Root cause of the ui-react vitest heap OOM found and confirmed fixed.

Root cause: `UIIntroduction`'s old props destructured default-array parameters (`anchorFallbackSelectors = []`, `additionalCutoutSelectors = []`). Default parameter expressions re-evaluate on every function call, so every render produced a brand-new empty-array reference. Those arrays flowed into `useMemo`/`useEffect` dependency arrays inside `useIntroductionAnchorRect`/`useIntroductionCutoutRects`, so those effects saw "changed deps" on every single render, re-ran, called `setState` with yet another fresh array reference, which triggered another render — an unbounded effect→render→effect cycle with no synchronous recursion for React's built-in "Maximum update depth exceeded" safeguard to catch. Confirmed empirically: isolating the single first `UIIntroduction` test (`cuts out the uncollapsed panel stamped with data-active-tab-id...`) reproduced the hang completely alone (CPU pegged >100%, RSS growing ~850MB/min, zero console output ever flushing — consistent with a microtask storm starving the event loop's I/O phase).

Investigation steps: instrumented `vitest.setup.ts` with per-test heap logging (`--reporter=verbose` was required — the default reporter swallows console output for passing tests) to prove test *collection* (registering all 327 tests) is fast/cheap (~5s, ~540MB) and the leak is purely in *execution* of one specific test's effect logic. Bisected the full run to the exact first hanging test and confirmed via code reading + isolated reproduction.

Resolution: a concurrent session (ticket UNIVERSAL-UI-ELEMENT-ID-SYSTEM) landed a refactor on this exact code mid-investigation, replacing the whole anchor-selector mechanism with a new `elementIdSelector`/`data-element-alias` system, which incidentally removed the unstable default-array parameters entirely. Re-verified: the full suite now completes in 8.64s (was 31+ min OOM before), 314/327 passing, 0 heap errors. The 13 remaining failures are unrelated — stale test fixtures still using the old `anchor`/`emphasis`/`cutouts` step shape instead of the new `introduce`/`show` shape from that other in-progress refactor; not a memory issue and not in this ticket's scope.

Reverted all temporary [DEBUG] instrumentation added to `vitest.setup.ts` and `index.tsx` during investigation — no debug code left in either file.
